legacy_inputs: S3 otterworks-file-storage, full listing of the files/ prefix
DynamoDB otterworks-file-metadata, full scan collecting referenced s3_key values
target_objects: Lambda function ow-tp-orphan-quarantine (on-demand, no provisioned concurrency)
EventBridge rule ow-tp-orphan-detect (event-driven, no schedule expression)
S3 event notification configuration on ow-tp-file-storage
S3 lifecycle configuration on ow-tp-file-quarantine (quarantine expiry)

acceptance_checks.description: The orphan set is compared against the baseline as a set of S3 keys, not a count: exactly the 4 seeded orphan objects (files/demo/orphan-000.bin .. orphan-003.bin) are quarantined.
The reverse orphan (metadata row reverse-orphan pointing at files/demo/missing-reverse.bin with no object present) is NOT quarantined and NOT deleted from metadata; asymmetry direction is preserved.
All 72 referenced objects survive: the post-run object listing of the storage bucket equals the baseline surviving-key set.

Quarantine is copy-then-delete with the same destination layout semantics as the baseline (dated quarantine prefix preserving the source key path), verified by listing the quarantine bucket through the S3 API.

The event-driven path is exercised live: creating an unreferenced object under the storage bucket's files/ prefix results in that object being quarantined without any scheduled invocation, and the quarantine decision is recorded in ow-tp-orphan-audit.

Lifecycle and notification configuration are read back from the AWS APIs (GetBucketNotificationConfiguration, GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration, EventBridge DescribeRule) rather than from Terraform state, and the EventBridge rule carries no schedule expression.
Replaying the same event is idempotent: an object already quarantined produces no duplicate quarantine object, no second audit row, and no error.
All resources are prefixed ow-tp-, tagged Project=otterworks-tp, and serverless/on-demand only; a tag/prefix scan after teardown returns nothing.

encoding_policy.byte_transparency: Object bodies are moved byte-for-byte; keys containing multi-byte or URL-escaped characters are resolved to the same object the legacy lister saw, with no re-encoding of the key on the copy destination.
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: Object content is treated as opaque bytes and never decoded; only keys and metadata are interpreted.

malformed_record_policy.details: A metadata item with a missing or empty s3_key must not cause its object to be treated as orphaned by omission: such items are attributed as unresolvable references and reported, and no deletion is performed on their behalf. Extra unmodeled attributes on a metadata item are ignored, never a reason to skip the row.

empty_input_semantics.details: Legacy explicitly still generated its savings report when zero orphans were found ('Still generate report even with 0 orphans'). The replacement must therefore keep an observable zero-orphan outcome for the period (an audit/metric record showing zero) rather than emitting nothing at all.

planted_anomalies.description: 4 objects under files/demo/ with no metadata row: orphan-000.bin, orphan-001.bin, orphan-002.bin, orphan-003.bin.
Metadata row reverse-orphan referencing a nonexistent object; must be left alone in both stores.
72 referenced objects that must survive the run unchanged.
The legacy report's dollar savings estimate is derived from a hardcoded per-GB rate.
planted_anomalies.reason: It is a presentation-only figure computed from the freed bytes, carries no operational meaning, and is not reproduced by configuration-based quarantine; freed bytes themselves are compared instead.

planted_anomalies.description: S3-event-driven quarantine happens within seconds of object creation rather than at a fixed daily instant, so no single batch boundary exists.
planted_anomalies.reason: Intended semantic change from daily sweep to per-object event. Live verification exercises the event path directly and compares the resulting orphan set, so the absence of a batch boundary does not weaken the reconciliation.
